answer: Persistent Operator Ledger. Each new identity must map to an operator key derived from shared infrastructure fingerprints (host, network path, signing habits) recorded in an atlas of operator history. When N identities converge on one operator, enforcement throttles that operator's aggregate throughput and raises the compute price for every wallet it runs; a gale of congestion, not a wallet freeze. Operators must forge distinct infrastructure to escape, costing real provisioning per identity and slow migration.
